body.statement: Let \(A,A':\mathcal H\to\mathcal G_a\) have closed range, reduced minimum moduli at least \(\mu>0\), and \(\varepsilon=\|A'-A\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\mu\). Then \[\operatorname{gap}(\ker A',\ker A)\le\varepsilon/\mu,\qquad \operatorname{gap}(\ker A'^*,\ker A^*)\le\varepsilon/\mu.\] With the symmetric gap convention for closed subspaces, the same bounds control the norms of the associated orthogonal-projection differences. Applied to \(A=\widetilde T_a(P)\) and \(A'=\widetilde T_a(P')\), operator-norm continuity and the uniform reduced-modulus bound therefore imply \(\|\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P')-\widetilde\Pi_{N,a}(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\) and \(\|\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P')-\widetilde\Pi_{K,a}(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\to0\). When these projections have finite rank, a bound below one also forces equality of their ranks, so fixed nullity and cokernel are locally redundant labels on such a component. No differentiability of projections or bridge selections, solvability-submanifold claim, or path-score realization follows from these bounds.
body.justification: The perturbation bound derives moving kernel and cokernel continuity from the spectral gap instead of maintaining those conclusions as assumptions.
body.gap: Standard closed-range perturbation arguments control subspace gaps, but they do not solve the proposal's reverse path-score lifting problem.
body.consumer: The lemma supplies stable transported null-space coordinates for the score-lifting construction and the finite-chart continuity arguments.
